story.opened: Established by 1760, according to Spitalfields Life and PubWiki.
story.then: A 2012 Spitalfields Life article says the pub was once a Truman's house and that Mr and Mrs Joel ran it from 1922 to 1955, keeping it open through the Second World War. Teresa Farnham called last orders after 21 years behind the bar in February 2012, with a new publican taking over that week. PubWiki notes an earlier address at 68 Columbia Road. Its current website is run by Urban Pubs & Bars.
story.now: The venue's own website lists a free comedy night every Wednesday (2nd Row Comedy, doors from 6:30pm), live music from a trad band in the main bar on the second Sunday of each month, and a Halloween event.
worth_knowing: Spitalfields Life says the name nods to the Huguenot habit of keeping caged birds, which spread through the East End.
Spitalfields Life says the pub defines the western edge of the Columbia Road flower market.
Spitalfields Life says the ornate flourish on top of the building may have been destroyed in the Second World War.
